pages.summary: Run tests and give their results; tests written as the local functions of a file.
body: `runtests` runs the tests of files, folders, classes or names (the current folder unless given), reports each failure as it happens and then a summary, and gives a result for each test: Name, Passed, Failed, Incomplete, Duration and Details. A function-based test file's main function returns `functiontests(localfunctions)`: its local functions whose names start or end with "test", each taking a test case to qualify with, and `setupOnce`, `teardownOnce`, `setup` and `teardown` run around them. `localfunctions` gives handles to the local functions of the file it is called in. Options choose tests by name (`'Name'`, wildcards allowed), take subfolders, and set how much is shown (`'OutputDetail'`).
syntax: Some of them, more or less told.
Handles to the file's local functions.

examples.title: A test file with a mistake in it
examples.code:
lines = ["function tests = squareTest"
    "tests = functiontests(localfunctions);"
    "end"
    "function testPositive(testCase)"
    "verifyEqual(testCase, 3^2, 9)"
    "end"
    "function testNegative(testCase)"
    "verifyEqual(testCase, (-3)^2, 9)"
    "end"
    "function testWrong(testCase)"
    "verifyEqual(testCase, 2^2, 5)"
    "end"];
writelines(lines, 'squareTest.m');
results = runtests('squareTest');
[results.Passed]
results(3).Name
examples.output:
Running squareTest
..
================================================================================
Verification failed in squareTest/testWrong.
    verifyEqual failed.
    --> The values differ: 1 of 1 element, the first at index 1, the largest difference 1.
    Actual:
        4
    Expected:
        5
================================================================================
.
Done squareTest
__________

Failure Summary:

     Name                  Failed  Incomplete  Reason(s)
    ========================================================
     squareTest/testWrong    X                 Failed by verification.
ans =

  1×3 logical array

   1   1   0

ans =

    'squareTest/testWrong'

pages.summary: Test suites: the tests to run, gathered now and run later.
body: A suite is an array of tests, each with its Name, made from the same things `runtests` takes: `testsuite` from files, folders, classes or names, and the `TestSuite` functions from one kind each. Suites can be indexed and concatenated, and run by `run` (with a runner or alone). A class-based test is a class derived from `matlab.unittest.TestCase` whose methods in a `(Test)` block are the tests; `(TestMethodSetup)` methods run before each.
syntax: From files, folders, classes or names.

examples.title: A test class, gathered three ways
examples.code:
lines = ["classdef StackTest < matlab.unittest.TestCase"
    "    properties"
    "        S"
    "    end"
    "    methods (TestMethodSetup)"
    "        function makeStack(tc)"
    "            tc.S = {};"
    "        end"
    "    end"
    "    methods (Test)"
    "        function startsEmpty(tc)"
    "            tc.verifyEmpty(tc.S)"
    "        end"
    "        function pushOne(tc)"
    "            tc.S{end+1} = 5;"
    "            tc.verifyNumElements(tc.S, 1)"
    "        end"
    "    end"
    "end"];
writelines(lines, 'StackTest.m');
suite = testsuite('StackTest');
{suite.Name}'
numel(matlab.unittest.TestSuite.fromClass(?StackTest))
one = matlab.unittest.TestSuite.fromName('StackTest/pushOne');
r = run(one);
r.Passed
examples.output:
ans = 

  2×1 cell array

    {'StackTest/startsEmpty'}
    {'StackTest/pushOne'}

ans =

     2

Running StackTest
.
Done StackTest
__________

ans =

  logical

   1

pages.summary: Test runners, which run a suite and report as they go or not at all, and a check that every test passed.
body: A runner made `withTextOutput` reports as `runtests` does; one made `withNoPlugins` runs silently, leaving only the results. `run(runner, suite)` runs the suite. `assertSuccess` throws an error naming the tests that failed, unless every one passed, so that a script or build stops there.

examples.title: Run quietly, then insist
examples.code:
lines = ["function tests = mathTest"
    "tests = functiontests(localfunctions);"
    "end"
    "function testSqrt(testCase)"
    "verifyEqual(testCase, sqrt(16), 4)"
    "end"
    "function testRound(testCase)"
    "verifyEqual(testCase, round(2.5), 2)"
    "end"];
writelines(lines, 'mathTest.m');
runner = matlab.unittest.TestRunner.withNoPlugins;
results = run(runner, testsuite('mathTest'));
[results.Passed]
try
    assertSuccess(results)
catch e
    disp(e.message)
end
examples.output:
ans =

  1×2 logical array

   1   0

1 of 2 tests failed or did not run to the end:
    mathTest/testRound

pages.summary: A test case to try qualifications at the prompt, and something to do when a test ends.
body: `forInteractiveUse` gives a test case whose qualifications print at once whether they passed, with the reason when not: a way to see what a check does before writing it into a test. In a test, `addTeardown` registers a function (with its arguments) to call when the test ends, passed or failed, the last added first: a test that changes something shared puts it back this way.
syntax: A test case at the prompt.

examples.title: Checks at the prompt
examples.output:
Verification passed.
Verification failed.
    verifyEqual failed.
    --> The values differ: 1 of 1 element, the first at index 1, the largest difference 5.55112e-17.
    Actual:
        0.3
    Expected:
        0.3

examples.title: A test that puts the display format back
examples.code:
lines = ["function tests = tidyTest"
    "tests = functiontests(localfunctions);"
    "end"
    "function testFormat(testCase)"
    "format long"
    "addTeardown(testCase, @format, 'short')"
    "addTeardown(testCase, @disp, 'teardown: format short again')"
    "verifyEqual(testCase, num2str(pi, 8), '3.1415927')"
    "end"];
writelines(lines, 'tidyTest.m');
r = runtests('tidyTest');
pi
examples.output:
Running tidyTest
teardown: format short again
.
Done tidyTest
__________

ans =

    3.1416

pages.summary: Qualifications that a value equals the expected one, or does not: the four kinds of check.
body: Every check comes in four kinds, which differ in what a failure does. A verification records the failure and the test goes on; an assertion ends the test there (the others still run); a fatal assertion ends the whole run; an assumption marks the test incomplete (filtered, not failed), for a test that cannot run here. Equality is of class, size and values (cell arrays, structs and objects compared element by element); `'AbsTol'` and `'RelTol'` allow a difference in numbers, either one sufficing. A failure tells what differs, and a text argument at the end is added to the report.
syntax: Equal, else the failure is recorded.
Equal, else the test is incomplete.

examples.title: Equal, nearly, and not at all
examples.code:
tc = matlab.unittest.TestCase.forInteractiveUse;
verifyEqual(tc, [1 2 3], [1 2 3])
verifyEqual(tc, int8(1), 1)
verifyEqual(tc, exp(log(5)), 5, 'RelTol', 1e-12)
verifyNotEqual(tc, 'abc', 'abd')
try
    assertEqual(tc, [1 2], [1 3], 'the second element')
catch e
    class(e)
end
examples.output:
Verification passed.
Verification failed.
    verifyEqual failed.
    --> The classes differ: int8 (actual) and double (expected).
    Actual:
        int8(1)
    Expected:
        1
Verification passed.
Verification passed.
Assertion failed.
    the second element
    assertEqual failed.
    --> The values differ: 1 of 2 elements, the first at index 2, the largest difference 1.
    Actual:
        [1 2]
    Expected:
        [1 3]
ans =

    'MException'

pages.summary: Qualifications that a value is true, or false.
body: The value must be a logical scalar: an array, or a number such as 1, fails even when every element is true (use `all` for an array). Verifications record a failure, assertions end the test, fatal assertions the run, and assumptions mark the test incomplete (see `verifyEqual`).
syntax: True, else the test is incomplete.

examples.title: Logical scalars only
examples.code:
tc = matlab.unittest.TestCase.forInteractiveUse;
verifyTrue(tc, isrow(1:3))
verifyFalse(tc, isempty(1:3))
verifyTrue(tc, 1)
verifyTrue(tc, all([true true]))
try
    assumeTrue(tc, ispc, 'needs Windows')
catch
    disp('the test would be incomplete here')
end
examples.output:
Verification passed.
Verification passed.
Verification failed.
    verifyTrue failed.
    --> The value is not a logical scalar.
    Actual:
        1
Verification passed.
Assumption failed.
    needs Windows
    assumeTrue failed.
    --> The value is false.
    Actual:
        false
the test would be incomplete here

pages.summary: Qualifications that a function throws an error, issues a warning, or issues none.
body: The function is given as a handle and called by the check. An error must carry the identifier given (or a meta.class of the exception); a warning must be among those issued, by identifier. `verifyWarningFree` passes when the function issues no warning at all. The warning checks give the function's outputs when asked for them. Verifications record a failure, assertions end the test, fatal assertions the run, assumptions mark it incomplete (see `verifyEqual`).

examples.title: An error, a warning, and neither
examples.code:
tc = matlab.unittest.TestCase.forInteractiveUse;
verifyError(tc, @() error('shop:empty', 'The basket is empty.'), 'shop:empty')
verifyError(tc, @() ones(2) * ones(3), 'shop:empty')
verifyWarning(tc, @() warning('shop:late', 'Delivery is late.'), 'shop:late')
v = verifyWarningFree(tc, @() sqrt(16))
examples.output:
Verification passed.
Verification failed.
    verifyError failed.
    --> The error thrown has the identifier 'MATLAB:innerdim'.
    Error thrown: MATLAB:innerdim: Incorrect dimensions for matrix multiplication. Check that the number of columns in the first matrix matches the number of rows in the second matrix. To operate on each element of the matrix individually, use TIMES (.*) for elementwise multiplication.
    Expected identifier: 'shop:empty'
Verification passed.
Verification passed.
v =

     4

pages.summary: Qualifications of a value's shape: empty or not, its size, length and number of elements.
body: `verifyEmpty` and `verifyNotEmpty` ask `isempty`; `verifySize` compares the whole size vector, `verifyLength` the largest dimension, and `verifyNumElements` the count of elements. Verifications record a failure, assertions end the test, fatal assertions the run, assumptions mark it incomplete (see `verifyEqual`).

examples.title: A 2-by-3 matrix
examples.code:
tc = matlab.unittest.TestCase.forInteractiveUse;
A = ones(2, 3);
verifySize(tc, A, [2 3])
verifyLength(tc, A, 3)
verifyNumElements(tc, A, 6)
verifyNotEmpty(tc, A)
verifyEmpty(tc, A(:, []))
verifySize(tc, A, [3 2])
examples.output:
Verification passed.
Verification passed.
Verification passed.
Verification passed.
Verification passed.
Verification failed.
    verifySize failed.
    --> The size is 2×3, not 3×2.

pages.summary: Qualifications of a value's class: exactly a class, or that class or one derived from it.
body: `verifyClass` asks that the value's class be exactly the one named (or a meta.class object); `verifyInstanceOf` also accepts subclasses, as `isa` does. Verifications record a failure, assertions end the test, fatal assertions the run, assumptions mark it incomplete (see `verifyEqual`).

examples.title: Numbers and handles
examples.output:
Verification passed.
Verification failed.
    verifyClass failed.
    --> The value's class is double.
Verification passed.
Verification passed.

pages.summary: Qualifications that every value is above a floor or below a ceiling.
body: Each element of the value is compared with the bound (a scalar, or an array of the value's size); every one must hold, and a failure names those that do not. Verifications record a failure, assertions end the test, fatal assertions the run, assumptions mark it incomplete (see `verifyEqual`).

examples.title: Probabilities
examples.output:
Verification passed.
Verification passed.
Verification failed.
    verifyGreaterThan failed.
    --> Not every value is greater than 0.25.
    Actual:
        [0.2 0.5 0.3]

pages.summary: Qualifications that a function, called with no inputs, gives true.
body: The function is given as a handle, and its result must be a logical scalar true. Writing the condition as a function lets the report show the function itself, which says more than a bare false would. Verifications record a failure, assertions end the test, fatal assertions the run, assumptions mark it incomplete (see `verifyEqual`).

examples.title: Conditions as functions
examples.output:
Verification passed.
Verification failed.
    verifyReturnsTrue failed.
    --> The function gave false.

pages.summary: Qualifications of text: that it holds a piece of text, or matches a regular expression.
body: `verifySubstring` asks that the text contain the piece exactly (case counts); `verifyMatches` that the regular expression match somewhere in it (anchor it with ^ and $ to match the whole). Verifications record a failure, assertions end the test, fatal assertions the run, assumptions mark it incomplete (see `verifyEqual`).

examples.title: A message and a code
examples.output:
Verification passed.
Verification failed.
    verifySubstring failed.
    --> The text does not contain 'Rows'.
    Actual:
        'Saved 12 rows to out.csv.'
Verification passed.

pages.summary: Qualifications that always fail: a test not written yet, or a branch that must not be reached.
body: They fail whatever happens, with the text given as the reason: a placeholder for a test still to be written, or a mark in a branch the code should never take. Verifications record a failure, assertions end the test, fatal assertions the run, assumptions mark it incomplete (see `verifyEqual`).

examples.title: A placeholder
examples.code:
tc = matlab.unittest.TestCase.forInteractiveUse;
verifyFail(tc, 'Test the empty input too.')
examples.output:
Verification failed.
    Test the empty input too.
    verifyFail failed.

pages.summary: Qualifications that two handles are the same object, or different ones.
body: Two handles to one object are the same however they were copied; two objects with equal contents are not. Verifications record a failure, assertions end the test, fatal assertions the run, assumptions mark it incomplete (see `verifyEqual`).

examples.title: A copy of a handle and a second map
examples.output:

Verification passed.
Verification failed.
    verifySameHandle failed.
    --> They are different objects.
